summary: Mono County stretches across 3,130 square miles of eastern Sierra Nevada high desert and alpine terrain yet holds fewer than 13,000 residents — a population density of roughly four people per square mile, making it one of the emptiest counties in California. That emptiness is the point: the landscape is dominated by the jagged Sierra crest to the west, the volcanic tablelands around Mono Lake, and peaks above 13,000 feet, delivering the kind of open-sky panoramas that most Californians drive hours to photograph on a long weekend. The median household income of about $87,000 sounds comfortable until you see a median home value above $514,000 — a price-to-income ratio near 5.9 — and realize the local economy leans heavily on tourism, recreation, outdoor services, and county government, with Mammoth Mountain as the dominant economic engine. Winters are genuinely cold: the annual average high is just 54°F, nighttime lows average 34°F year-round, and heavy snowfall defines months of daily life, though 9.4 hours of average daily sunshine keep the sky bright even in January. Grocery and dining options are limited to a handful of small-town clusters rather than any real commercial corridor. Mono is a place where the commute might be spectacular — and the tradeoff is that almost everything else requires a long drive.
